summary: Flathead NF 90-ft steel Aermotor tower built 1949 beside the old Condon Ranger Station; gone by 1975, while the station residence is now a rental cabin.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says gone by 1975; Forest Lookouts lists it as Removed. The 1920s station compound survives and is rented.

access.note: The restored ranger residence is rented year-round through Recreation.gov. No source describes access to the tower site, which is gone.

visit.trail_note: Drive from Highway 83 along Condon Loop Road 124 to the rental cabin. The tower itself is gone.

events.note: Forest Service photo captioned as taken from the Condon lookout tower; the tower stood then
Gone by 1975; no removal date or cause given

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Record has two points: the FFLA point (47.5847, -113.7361) and a west_us_lookouts point (47.5356, -113.7195) about 5.6 km south. The Forest Service coordinates for Old Condon Ranger Station (47.58509, -113.73738) match the FFLA point, so the FFLA point is kept. The southern point is already hidden as a merged duplicate.

sources.title: A worthless lot of shacks: Ranger Stations of the Swan Valley

notes_for_editor: Tower-specific detail is thin: firelookout.com gives the build year, height and gone-by-1975; the other lookout pages only say Removed or Tower Gone. Station and rental facts come from the Forest Service page and a rental blog. Height 27.4 m is converted from 90 ft. The Bigfork Eagle 1956 caption is the only evidence the tower stood after 1949 apart from the 1975 cutoff. The Montana Ranger Stations correction names the truck shed date but gives no tower date. No source describes the tower footings today.
